svg.title: 4. Inspection and egress with Network Firewall
svg.text: Firewall policy: stateful, strict order, default action drop established + alert established
DNS and the things people forget
Inspection VPC: Transit Gateway route tables send every packet between trust zones, and every packet to the internet, through Network Firewall
no propagations, so spokes never see each other
this is the return path after inspection
Return path: public subnet RT sends 10.0.0.0/8 to the
same-AZ firewall endpoint, then TGW, then the firewall RT
picks the spoke. Both directions are inspected.
1. deny prod <-> non-prod by CIDR (belt and braces with the blackhole route)
2. allow core -> CDE tokenizer on TCP 443 only, from two named subnets
3. egress allow-list: 38 FQDNs matched on TLS SNI and HTTP Host (domain list rule group)
4. Suricata: drop TLS without SNI, drop non-TLS on 443, drop DNS over HTTPS resolvers
5. AWS managed threat signature groups (malware, botnet, emerging events) in drop mode
Alert and flow logs to S3 in the log archive account, then Security Lake.
Every rule change ships through a pipeline with a test VPC, alert mode first.
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall on every VPC: block known-bad lists,
Advanced rules for DNS tunnelling and DGA domains, alert on everything else.
Appliance mode keeps both directions of a flow in one AZ. Without it,
return traffic can land on the other AZ firewall and be dropped as asymmetric.
One firewall endpoint and one NAT gateway per AZ: losing an AZ loses only
that AZ, not every egress flow in the Region.
